# Aggregate light-fiber mass does not force a circuit contact into the body

This is an exact obstruction to strengthening the product-source contact
test by total source volume alone. It remains an obstruction when the
barycentric coefficients are all equal, or are the actual mixed-volume
weights, and when their maximum tends to zero. Every source is an
actual positive integer fiber of one convex body. The circuit has full
continuous rank. Its total cap budget can be below OC, but the circuit
does not cover all of S; this is not an OC counterexample.

## 1. An actual convex family with many individually light fibers

Fix d>=1 and an integer s>=2, and put

  m=2s^d,   Q=[-1/2,1/2]^d,   Q_s=Q/s.

Use two integer coordinates z=(j,h). Define the full-dimensional
convex body

  C=[0,m-1] x conv(({0} x Q) union ({1} x Q_s)).           (1)

The factor order is (j,h,x). Its integer fibers are exactly

  K_(j,0)=Q,       K_(j,1)=Q_s,       j=0,...,m-1.         (2)

They have volumes 1 and s^(-d), respectively. Consequently

  M=m(1+s^(-d))=2(s^d+1).                               (3)

At a real height 0<=h<=1 its continuous fiber is

  [(1-h)+h/s] Q,                                        (4)

by exact Minkowski interpolation of the two homothetic endpoint
cubes. There are no omitted integer fibers, and H_d is precisely the
finite mixed-volume sum.

## 2. One full-rank circuit with an arbitrary real contact height

Choose any theta in (0,1). Let

  u_i=e_i (1<=i<=d),      u_0=-sum_(i=1)^d e_i,
  y=d e_1,
  A=4(d+1)/[theta(1-theta)].

Define d+1 ambient caps by the affine margins

  L_i(j,h,x)=u_i.(x-h y/theta)+A(h-theta),
  H_i={L_i>=0}.                                         (5)

Their continuous normals form a minimal positive dependence with
equal weights 1/(d+1), span rank d, and have nonzero continuous part.
They concur at every point with h=theta and x=y. In particular use

  q=((m-1)/2, theta; y).                                 (6)

The common integer term is A(h-theta), so the caps cover the full
continuous space above h>theta. They do not cover the bottom fibers.

On a bottom fiber, every margin satisfies

  L_i <= d/2-A theta
       =d/2-4(d+1)/(1-theta)<0.                         (7)

On a top fiber, every margin satisfies

  L_i >= -d/(2s)-d/theta+A(1-theta)
       =-d/(2s)+(3d+4)/theta>0.                         (8)

Here |u_i.y|<=d and the cube support magnitudes are at most d/2
and d/(2s), so the estimates hold for all d+1 normals. They are
strict and keep every closed-cap boundary away from the integer
fibers. Thus each cap misses every bottom fiber and contains every
top fiber, and has EXACT total mixed mass

  mu(H_i)=m s^(-d)=2=:T.                                (9)

Every individual fiber volume is strictly smaller than T, and in
particular strictly smaller than T/gamma_d. Nevertheless

  M/T=s^d+1 -> infinity.                                (10)

The point q is strictly outside C: its first continuous coordinate
is d>=1, whereas every continuous coordinate in C is at most 1/2.
The same is true for every Minkowski interpolant of the original
fibers. This is actual geometric nonmembership, not failure of a
prescribed formula to identify a point.

For all s with s^d+1>4/gamma_d, every cap fraction in (9) is below
gamma_d/4, the OC target for n=2. The bottom fibers are still missed
by the entire circuit. Therefore this observation supplies no
global bad-cap cover and no contradiction to OC.

## 3. Uniform coefficients and actual volume coefficients both work

First choose equal coefficients t_z=1/(2m) on all 2m sources. Their
base mean is ((m-1)/2,1/2). Set theta=1/2 in (5). Then (6) is
exactly the corresponding real contact base. The actual continuous
Minkowski interpolant is ((1+1/s)/2)Q, which does not contain y.
All coefficients are equal and their maximum tends to zero.

Alternatively use the true volume barycentric coefficients

  t_(j,0)=1/M,
  t_(j,1)=s^(-d)/M.

Their base mean is

  ((m-1)/2, theta),     theta=1/(s^d+1).                 (11)

Use this theta in (5). Again (6) has exactly this mean base. The
Minkowski interpolant is

  [(s^d+1/s)/(s^d+1)] Q,                                (12)

and does not contain y. In this version max_z t_z=1/[2(s^d+1)]
tends to zero, sum t_z w_z tends to one, and the inverse-square
effective number 1/sum t_z^2 tends to infinity. None of these
aggregate or diffuse-coefficient conditions prevents the external
contact. The full mixed centroid has continuous coordinate zero;
only the contact's BASE equals the true base mean.

## 4. The exact convolution and the source of the obstruction

For either of these coefficient choices, let X_z be independent
uniform source points and put X_bar=sum t_z X_z. Formula (3) of
`candidate 203262a6491295f6` gives the
lifted margin

  sum_z t_z L_i(z,X_z)=u_i.(X_bar-y).                    (13)

Always X_bar belongs to Q. Consequently the lifted cap for u_0
contains the ENTIRE product body:

  u_0.(X_bar-y)=d-sum_l X_bar,l >=d/2>0.                 (14)

The lifted u_1 cap is empty, since X_bar,1-d<=1/2-d<0.
For i>=2 the lifted cap probability is exactly 1/2: the weighted
coordinate sum is symmetric and has an atom-free distribution.
All source marginals are uniform intervals or cubes, so their
affine margin laws and their convolutions are log-concave.

For every original cap, however, its fractional source masses are
zero on each bottom source and one on each top source. The product
union bound is therefore EXACT for cap 0: its independent union
probability and its lifted cap probability are both one, and its
defect Delta_0 is zero. For cap 1 the defect is one; for the other
caps it is one half. There is no unaccounted boundary mass.

The integer tilt in (5) grows when theta is small. Thus the tiny
volume-weighted top coefficients do not suppress their scalar
margin contribution: the actual positive margins grow by the
reciprocal height scale. Formula (13) tracks this exactly. A
convolution argument based solely on cap fractions, source masses,
or the diffuseness of t cannot discard that scale information.

This closes an aggregate-weight-only inference for one circuit,
even with full rank, actual uniform source marginals, true base-mean
coefficients, and cap fractions below the global target. It leaves
open a bound using additional simultaneous circuits or quantified
margin widths, rather than their untracked normalization.
